agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# zk configuration file
#
# Uncomment the properties you want to customize.

# NOTE SETTINGS
#
# Defines the default options used when generating new notes.
[note]

# Language used when writing notes.
# This is used to generate slugs or with date formats.
#language = "en"

# The default title used for new note, if no `--title` flag is provided.
#default-title = "Untitled"

# Template used to generate a note's filename, without extension.
#filename = "{{id}}"

# The file extension used for the notes.
#extension = "md"

# Template used to generate a note's content.
# If not an absolute path or "~/unix/path", it's relative to .zk/templates/
template = "default.md"

# Path globs ignored while indexing existing notes.
#exclude = [
#    "drafts/*",
#    "log.md"
#]

# Configure random ID generation.

# The charset used for random IDs. You can use:
#   * letters: only letters from a to z.
#   * numbers: 0 to 9
#   * alphanum: letters + numbers
#   * hex: hexadecimal, from a to f and 0 to 9
#   * custom string: will use any character from the provided value
#id-charset = "alphanum"

# Length of the generated IDs.
#id-length = 4

# Letter case for the random IDs, among lower, upper or mixed.
#id-case = "lower"


# EXTRA VARIABLES
#
# A dictionary of variables you can use for any custom values when generating
# new notes. They are accessible in templates with {{extra.<key>}}
[extra]

#key = "value"


# GROUP OVERRIDES
#
# You can override global settings from [note] and [extra] for a particular
# group of notes by declaring a [group."<name>"] section.
#
# Specify the list of directories which will automatically belong to the group
# with the optional `paths` property.
#
# Omitting `paths` is equivalent to providing a single path equal to the name of
# the group. This can be useful to quickly declare a group by the name of the
# directory it applies to.

#[group."<NAME>"]
#paths = ["<DIR1>", "<DIR2>"]
#[group."<NAME>".note]
#filename = "{{format-date now}}"
#[group."<NAME>".extra]
#key = "value"


# MARKDOWN SETTINGS
[format.markdown]

# Format used to generate links between notes.
# Either "wiki", "markdown" or a custom template. Default is "markdown".
link-format = "wiki"
# Indicates whether a link's path will be percent-encoded.
# Defaults to true for "markdown" format and false for "wiki" format.
#link-encode-path = true
# Indicates whether a link's path file extension will be removed.
# Defaults to true.
#link-drop-extension = true

# Enable support for #hashtags.
hashtags = true
# Enable support for :colon:separated:tags:.
colon-tags = false
# Enable support for Bear's #multi-word tags#
# Hashtags must be enabled for multi-word tags to work.
multiword-tags = false


# EXTERNAL TOOLS
[tool]

# Default editor used to open notes. When not set, the EDITOR or VISUAL
# environment variables are used.
#editor = "vim"

# Pager used to scroll through long output. If you want to disable paging
# altogether, set it to an empty string "".
#pager = "less -FIRX"

# Command used to preview a note during interactive fzf mode.
# Set it to an empty string "" to disable preview.

# bat is a great tool to render Markdown document with syntax highlighting.
#https://github.com/sharkdp/bat
#fzf-preview = "bat -p --color always {-1}"


# LSP
#
#   Configure basic editor integration for LSP-compatible editors.
#   See https://zk-org.github.io/zk/tips/editors-integration.html
#
[lsp]

[lsp.diagnostics]
# Each diagnostic can have for value: none, hint, info, warning, error

# Report titles of wiki-links as hints.
#wiki-title = "hint"
# Warn for dead links between notes.
dead-link = "error"
# Warn when a note links to itself.
#self-link = "warning"
# Report missing backlinks
#missing-backlink = { level = "hint", position = "bottom" }


[lsp.completion]
# Customize the completion pop-up of your LSP client.

# Show the note title in the completion pop-up, or fallback on its path if empty.
#note-label = "{{title-or-path}}"
# Filter out the completion pop-up using the note title or its path.
#note-filter-text = "{{title}} {{path}}"
# Show the note filename without extension as detail.
#note-detail = "{{filename-stem}}"


# NAMED FILTERS
#
#    A named filter is a set of note filtering options used frequently together.
#
[filter]

# Matches the notes created the last two weeks. For example:
#    $ zk list recents --limit 15
#    $ zk edit recents --interactive
#recents = "--sort created- --created-after 'last two weeks'"


# COMMAND ALIASES
#
#   Aliases are user commands called with `zk <alias> [<flags>] [<args>]`.
#
#   The alias will be executed with `$SHELL -c`, please refer to your shell's
#   man page to see the available syntax. In most shells:

{"command":"EXEC=/workspace/executable
rm -rf /tmp/nb && mkdir /tmp/nb && cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC init --no-input
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC new --print-path --no-input --title "first note" 2>&1
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC new --print-path --no-input --title "second" 2>&1
ls /tmp/nb
cat /tmp/nb/*.md

# Let's investigate id charset & length
cd /tmp/nb && cat .zk/config.toml | grep -E "id-"
# Try changing config
cat > /tmp/nb/.zk/config.toml <<'EOF'
[note]
id-charset = "letters"
id-length = 6
id-case = "lower"
[format.markdown]
link-format = "wiki"
hashtags = true
EOF
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC new --print-path --no-input --title "custom id" 2>&1
ls /tmp/nb

# Test template functions for note filename
cat > /tmp/nb/.zk/config.toml <<'EOF'
[note]
filename = "{{slug title}}"
extension = "md"
template = "default.md"
id-charset = "alphanum"
id-length = 4
id-case = "lower"

[format.markdown]
link-format = "wiki"
hashtags = true
EOF
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC new --dry-run --no-input --title "Hello World" 2>&1
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC new --print-path --no-input --title "Hello World" 2>&1
ls /tmp/nb/*.md | tail -n 5
cat /tmp/nb/hello-world.md

# test group override
mkdir -p /tmp/nb/daily
cat > /tmp/nb/.zk/config.toml <<'EOF'
[note]
filename = "{{id}}"
extension = "md"
template = "default.md"

[format.markdown]
link-format = "wiki"
hashtags = true

[group."daily"]
paths = ["daily"]

[group."daily".note]
filename = "{{format-date now \"%Y-%m-%d\"}}"
EOF
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC new --dry-run --no-input --title "daily note" daily 2>&1
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC new --print-path --no-input --title "daily note" daily 2>&1
ls /tmp/nb/daily/

# Test index --force etc
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC index --help 2>&1
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC index --verbose 2>&1
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC index --force --verbose 2>&1

# Test edit help - does it just open editor? we should not run interactive
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC edit --help 2>&1

# list with all filters: we need to discover all
cd /tmp/nb && $EXEC list --help 2>&1 | tr '\n' '|' | tr -s '|' '\n' | head -n 200
"}

import subprocess, os
EXEC="/workspace/executable"
def run(args):
    proc=subprocess.run([EXEC]+args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    combined=proc.stdout+proc.stderr
    # Actually warnings go to stderr
    return proc.stderr, proc.stdout, proc.returncode

def test(wd, nd):
    cmd=[]
    if wd:
        cmd+=["--working-dir", wd]
    if nd:
        cmd+=["--notebook-dir", nd]
    cmd+=["list"]
    err,out,code = run(cmd)

def print_stderr(s):
    sys.stderr.write(s + "\n")

def error_exit(msg, code=1):
    print_stderr(msg)
    sys.exit(code)

def warning_lstat(path):
    print_stderr(f"zk: warning: lstat {path}: no such file or directory")

# Notebook discovery helpers
def first_missing_component(p):
    """Given absolute path string, return first component that doesn't exist, or None if all exist."""
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    # Build from root
    parts = pathlib.Path(p).parts
    # parts[0] is '/' for absolute
    cur = parts[0]
    # Check existence of each level
    # We need to check cur first? For absolute, cur is '/' exists.
    # Then iteratively join
    built = cur
    # For Unix, parts[0]='/', then e.g., 'tmp', 'nb', 'x'
    # So iterate index 1..
    for comp in parts[1:]:
        built = os.path.join(built, comp)
        # check existence
        try:
            os.lstat(built)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return built
        except Exception:
            # other error? treat as missing? but we only care FileNotFound
            # For other errors, we can still treat as missing? But to match original, only no such file triggers warning.
            pass
    return None

def existing_parent(p):
    """Return longest existing parent of p, or None if none exists (should at least / exists)"""
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    cur = pathlib.Path(p)
    while True:
        if os.path.exists(cur):
            return str(cur)
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

def is_notebook_dir(path):
    return os.path.isdir(os.path.join(path, ".zk"))

def find_notebook_in_ancestors(start_path):
    """Walk up from start_path looking for .zk directory. Return notebook path or None."""
    cur = pathlib.Path(os.path.abspath(start_path))
    # If start_path is file, use its parent? For notebook discovery, we use directory.
    if cur.is_file():
        cur = cur.parent
    # Walk up
    while True:
        if is_notebook_dir(str(cur)):
            return str(cur)
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

def wd_path_abs_resolved(wd_path, original_cwd, notebook_path):
    """Return effective working dir absolute path, for path calculations."""
    if wd_path is None:
        return original_cwd
    if os.path.isabs(wd_path):
        return os.path.abspath(wd_path)
    else:
        return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(original_cwd, wd_path))

# Config handling
def load_config(notebook_path):
    config_path = os.path.join(notebook_path, ".zk", "config.toml")
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        # No config? Use defaults
        return {}
    try:
        with open(config_path, "rb") as f:
            data = tomli.load(f)
            return data
    except Exception as e:
        # If parsing fails, return empty? But original would error with "failed to read config"
        # We need to handle duplicated tables error earlier: we saw error "failed to read config: (8, 2): duplicated tables"
        # That error message format suggests toml parsing error with line,col.
        # For our purposes, we will try to parse and if fails, we should error similar? Let's just error with generic?
        # To match original, we should use tomli which gives error with line/col.
        # We need to capture tomli error and format similar: "zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: (line, col): msg"
        # Let's attempt.
        try:
            with open(config_path, "rb") as f:
                tomli.load(f)
        except tomli.TOMLDecodeError as ex:
            # ex.args may contain line col?
            # tomli error message includes "at line X col Y"
            msg = str(ex)
            # Extract line col?
            # tomli's message: "Duplicate keys ... at line 8 col 2" etc.
            # We need to produce "(8, 2): duplicated tables" format as observed.
            # Let's try to parse
            # For duplicated tables, tomli says "Duplicate table ..."?
            # We'll attempt to produce similar.
            # For now, just forward message with our formatting attempt
            # Original error: "zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: (8, 2): duplicated tables"
            # We'll try to extract line col from ex
            line = getattr(ex, 'lineno', '?')
            col = getattr(ex, 'colno', '?')
            # If tomli doesn't have, try regex
            m = re.search(r'line (\d+) col (\d+)', str(ex))
            if m:
                line = m.group(1)
                col = m.group(2)
                # remainder message after?
                # For duplicated tables, message is "Duplicate keys..." but original says "duplicated tables"
                # We can try to produce message as "duplicated tables" if duplicate?
                if "duplicate" in str(ex).lower():
                    err_msg = "duplicated tables"
                else:
                    err_msg = str(ex).split(" at line")[0]
                error_exit(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: ({line}, {col}): {err_msg}")
            else:
                error_exit(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: {ex}")
        error_exit(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: {e}")

def get_note_config(config, group_name=None, dir_path=None):
    """Get effective note config considering group overrides."""
    # Defaults
    note_cfg = {
        "language": "en",
        "default-title": "Untitled",
        "filename": "{{id}}",
        "extension": "md",
        "template": "default.md",
        # "exclude": [],
        "id-charset": "alphanum",
        "id-length": 4,
        "id-case": "lower",
    }
    extra = {}
    # From config
    if "note" in config:
        for k,v in config["note"].items():
            note_cfg[k] = v
    if "extra" in config:
        extra = config["extra"].copy()
    # Markdown settings
    md_cfg = {
        "link-format": "wiki",
        "link-encode-path": None, # default depends on format
        "link-drop-extension": None,
        "hashtags": True,
        "colon-tags": False,
        "multiword-tags": False,
    }
    if "format" in config and "markdown" in config["format"]:
        for k,v in config["format"]["markdown"].items():
            md_cfg[k.replace("-", "_")] = v
            # also keep original hyphen version
            md_cfg[k] = v

    # Group handling
    effective_group = None
    if group_name:
        effective_group = group_name
    elif dir_path:
        # Check groups for matching paths
        # dir_path is relative dir from notebook root? We need to check
        # dir_path could be like "daily", "sub/dir", etc.
        # For each group, get its paths list, or default to group name
        groups = config.get("group", {})
        for gname, gdata in groups.items():
            # gdata may be dict
            paths = []
            if isinstance(gdata, dict) and "paths" in gdata:
                paths = gdata["paths"]
            else:
                paths = [gname]
            # Normalize paths: remove trailing slash
            for p in paths:
                # Simple glob matching: if dir_path == p or dir_path starts with p + "/"
                # Also support fnmatch?
                if dir_path == p or dir_path.startswith(p.rstrip("/") + "/"):
                    effective_group = gname
                    break
                # Also fnmatch
                if fnmatch.fnmatch(dir_path, p):
                    effective_group = gname
                    break
            if effective_group:
                break

    if effective_group:
        groups = config.get("group", {})
        if effective_group not in groups:
            error_exit(f"zk: error: new note: no group named `{effective_group}` found in the config")
        gdata = groups[effective_group]
        # Override note settings
        if isinstance(gdata, dict):
            if "note" in gdata:
                for k,v in gdata["note"].items():
                    note_cfg[k] = v
            if "extra" in gdata:
                for k,v in gdata["extra"].items():
                    extra[k] = v
            # Also if group has top-level note settings? In TOML, [group."name".note] is nested as group->name->note, we handled.
            # What about [group.mygroup] having paths? That's already used.

    # Return note_cfg, extra, md_cfg, effective_group
    return note_cfg, extra, md_cfg, effective_group

# Template rendering - minimal handlebars subset
class TemplateError(Exception):
    pass

def slugify(s):
    # Normalize unicode to ascii
    s = s.strip()
    # Remove diacritics
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', s)
    s = ''.join(c for c in s if unicodedata.category(c) != 'Mn')
    s = s.lower()
    # Replace non-alphanum with hyphen, but keep hyphen?
    # Replace any sequence of non-alphanumeric with hyphen
    s = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', s)
    s = s.strip('-')
    s = re.sub(r'-+', '-', s)
    return s

def render_template(template_str, context, config_md=None):
    """
    Render template with minimal helpers.
    context: dict with keys ID, Title, Content, Dir, Filename, FilenameStem, Extra, Now, Env, etc.
    Also supports lower/title etc? But we will only support helpers that are functional in original and return non-empty: slug, prepend, json, format-date, format-link, style, env, now, date (deprecated)
    Plus variables: id, title, content, dir, filename, filename-stem, path, abs-path, title-or-path, etc (but for new, path empty)
    For custom link-format template, context for format-link may have path, title.
    We'll implement a simple parser for {{...}} and {{#if ...}} etc? That's complex.
    For simplicity, we will support:

def get_id_charset(name):
    if name == "letters":
        return "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    elif name == "numbers":
        return "0123456789"
    elif name == "alphanum":
        return "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
    elif name == "hex":
        return "0123456789abcdef"
    else:
        return name  # custom

def generate_id(charset_name, length, case):
    base = get_id_charset(charset_name)
    result = []
    for _ in range(length):
        ch = random.choice(base)
        if ch.isalpha():
            if case == "lower":
                ch = ch.lower()
            elif case == "upper":
                ch = ch.upper()
            elif case == "mixed":
                ch = random.choice([ch.lower(), ch.upper()])
        result.append(ch)
    return "".join(result)

            except:

                                items = [x.strip().strip('"').strip("'") for x in inner.split(",") if x.strip()]

def print_stderr(s):
    sys.stderr.write(s + "\n")

def error_exit(msg, code=1):
    print_stderr(msg)
    sys.exit(code)

def warning_lstat(path):
    print_stderr(f"zk: warning: lstat {path}: no such file or directory")

# Notebook discovery helpers
def first_missing_component(p):
    """Given absolute path string, return first component that doesn't exist, or None if all exist."""
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    # Build from root
    parts = pathlib.Path(p).parts
    # parts[0] is '/' for absolute
    cur = parts[0]
    # Check existence of each level
    # We need to check cur first? For absolute, cur is '/' exists.
    # Then iteratively join
    built = cur
    # For Unix, parts[0]='/', then e.g., 'tmp', 'nb', 'x'
    # So iterate index 1..
    for comp in parts[1:]:
        built = os.path.join(built, comp)
        # check existence
        try:
            os.lstat(built)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return built
        except Exception:
            # other error? treat as missing? but we only care FileNotFound
            # For other errors, we can still treat as missing? But to match original, only no such file triggers warning.
            pass
    return None

def existing_parent(p):
    """Return longest existing parent of p, or None if none exists (should at least / exists)"""
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    cur = pathlib.Path(p)
    while True:
        if os.path.exists(cur):
            return str(cur)
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

def is_notebook_dir(path):
    return os.path.isdir(os.path.join(path, ".zk"))

def find_notebook_in_ancestors(start_path):
    """Walk up from start_path looking for .zk directory. Return notebook path or None."""
    cur = pathlib.Path(os.path.abspath(start_path))
    # If start_path is file, use its parent? For notebook discovery, we use directory.
    if cur.is_file():
        cur = cur.parent
    # Walk up
    while True:
        if is_notebook_dir(str(cur)):
            return str(cur)
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

def wd_path_abs_resolved(wd_path, original_cwd, notebook_path):
    """Return effective working dir absolute path, for path calculations."""
    if wd_path is None:
        return original_cwd
    if os.path.isabs(wd_path):

    else:
        return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(original_cwd, wd_path))

# Config handling
def load_config(notebook_path):
    config_path = os.path.join(notebook_path, ".zk", "config.toml")
    if not os.path.exists(config_path):
        # No config? Use defaults
        return {}
    try:
        with open(config_path, "rb") as f:
            data = tomli.load(f)
            return data
    except Exception as e:
        # If parsing fails, return empty? But original would error with "failed to read config"
        # We need to handle duplicated tables error earlier: we saw error "failed to read config: (8, 2): duplicated tables"
        # That error message format suggests toml parsing error with line,col.
        # For our purposes, we will try to parse and if fails, we should error similar? Let's just error with generic?
        # To match original, we should use tomli which gives error with line/col.
        # We need to capture tomli error and format similar: "zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: (line, col): msg"
        # Let's attempt.
        try:
            with open(config_path, "rb") as f:
                tomli.load(f)
        except tomli.TOMLDecodeError as ex:
            # ex.args may contain line col?
            # tomli error message includes "at line X col Y"
            msg = str(ex)
            # Extract line col?
            # tomli's message: "Duplicate keys ... at line 8 col 2" etc.
            # We need to produce "(8, 2): duplicated tables" format as observed.
            # Let's try to parse
            # For duplicated tables, tomli says "Duplicate table ..."?
            # We'll attempt to produce similar.
            # For now, just forward message with our formatting attempt
            # Original error: "zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: (8, 2): duplicated tables"
            # We'll try to extract line col from ex
            line = getattr(ex, 'lineno', '?')
            col = getattr(ex, 'colno', '?')
            # If tomli doesn't have, try regex
            m = re.search(r'line (\d+) col (\d+)', str(ex))
            if m:
                line = m.group(1)
                col = m.group(2)
                # remainder message after?
                # For duplicated tables, message is "Duplicate keys..." but original says "duplicated tables"
                # We can try to produce message as "duplicated tables" if duplicate?
                if "duplicate" in str(ex).lower():
                    err_msg = "duplicated tables"
                else:
                    err_msg = str(ex).split(" at line")[0]
                error_exit(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: ({line}, {col}): {err_msg}")
            else:
                error_exit(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: {ex}")
        error_exit(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: {e}")

    extra = {}

    if "note" in config:

    if "extra" in config:

    # Markdown settings
    md_cfg = {

        "link-drop-extension": None,
        "hashtags": True,

    if "format" in config and "markdown" in config["format"]:
        for k,v in config["format"]["markdown"].items():
            md_cfg[k.replace("-", "_")] = v
            # also keep original hyphen version
            md_cfg[k] = v

    # Group handling
    effective_group = None
    if group_name:

    elif dir_path:

    s = s.strip()
    # Remove diacritics
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', s)
    s = ''.join(c for c in s if unicodedata.category(c) != 'Mn')

    return s

def parse_extra(extra_list):
    """Parse --extra flags which can be repeated and each can contain comma-separated KEY=VALUE"""
    extra = {}
    if not extra_list:
        return extra
    for item in extra_list:
        # item may be "foo=bar,baz=qux"
        parts = item.split(",")
        for p in parts:
            if "=" in p:
                k,v = p.split("=",1)
                extra[k]=v
    return extra

# ID generation
def get_id_charset(name):
    if name == "letters":
        return "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    elif name == "numbers":
        return "0123456789"
    elif name == "alphanum":
        return "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
    elif name == "hex":
        return "0123456789abcdef"
    else:
        return name  # custom

def generate_id(charset_name, length, case):
    base = get_id_charset(charset_name)
    result = []
    for _ in range(length):
        ch = random.choice(base)
        if ch.isalpha():
            if case == "lower":
                ch = ch.lower()
            elif case == "upper":
                ch = ch.upper()
            elif case == "mixed":
                ch = random.choice([ch.lower(), ch.upper()])
        result.append(ch)
    return "".join(result)

            except:
                # Minimal parser
                # Attempt to parse simple key: value
                meta = {}
                current_key = None
                list_mode = False
                list_items = []
                for line in lines[1:end_idx]:

                    if not stripped:

                    if list_mode:

                        else:

                            if current_key:

                            list_mode = False
                            list_items = []
                            current_key = None
                    if ":" in line:
                        # key: value
                        # Split on first colon
                        k, v = line.split(":",1)
                        k = k.strip()
                        v = v.strip()
                        if v == "":

                            list_mode = True

                        else:

                                meta[k] = v
                if list_mode and current_key:

                metadata = meta

            body_content = remaining.lstrip("\n")
            # If body_content starts with "---\n"? No, that's frontmatter end already consumed.

def stderr(s):
    sys.stderr.write(s + "\n")

def error(msg, code=1):
    stderr(msg)
    sys.exit(code)

def warn_lstat(p):
    stderr(f"zk: warning: lstat {p}: no such file or directory")

def first_missing(p):
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    parts = pathlib.Path(p).parts
    cur = parts[0]
    built = cur
    for comp in parts[1:]:
        built = os.path.join(built, comp)
        try:
            os.lstat(built)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return built
    return None

def existing_parent(p):
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    cur = pathlib.Path(p)
    while True:
        if os.path.exists(cur):
            return str(cur)
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

def is_notebook(path):
    return os.path.isdir(os.path.join(path, ".zk"))

def find_notebook(start):
    cur = pathlib.Path(os.path.abspath(start))
    if cur.is_file():
        cur = cur.parent
    while True:
        if is_notebook(str(cur)):
            return str(cur)
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

def abs_from_cwd(p, cwd):
    if os.path.isabs(p):
        return os.path.abspath(p)
    return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(cwd, p))

def resolve_notebook(nd, wd, cwd):
    # Returns (notebook_path, effective_wd)
    # Logic matching earlier observations
    def resolve_wd_missing(wd_abs):
        missing = first_missing(wd_abs)
        return missing

    # ND present
    if nd is not None:
        nd_abs = abs_from_cwd(nd, cwd)
        nd_missing = first_missing(nd_abs)
        if nd_missing:
            parent = existing_parent(nd_abs)
            nb = find_notebook(parent) if parent else None
            # need WD warnings?
            wd_abs = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd) if wd else None
            wd_missing = first_missing(wd_abs) if wd_abs else None
            if nb:
                # success, ND valid (inside notebook)
                warn_lstat(nd_missing)
                warn_lstat(nd_missing)
                if wd_missing:
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                eff_wd = wd_abs if wd_abs else cwd
                return nb, eff_wd
            else:
                # fail
                warn_lstat(nd_missing)
                warn_lstat(nd_missing)
                if wd_missing:
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {nd} or a parent directory")
        else:
            # ND exists
            nb = find_notebook(nd_abs)
            if nb:
                # success
                if wd:
                    wd_abs = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd)
                    wd_missing = first_missing(wd_abs)
                    if wd_missing:
                        warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                        warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                eff_wd = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd) if wd else cwd
                return nb, eff_wd
            else:
                # no notebook in ND ancestors
                if wd:
                    wd_abs = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd)
                    wd_missing = first_missing(wd_abs)
                    if wd_missing:
                        warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {nd} or a parent directory")
    else:
        # No ND
        if wd:
            wd_abs = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd)
            wd_missing = first_missing(wd_abs)
            if wd_missing:
                parent = existing_parent(wd_abs)
                nb = find_notebook(parent) if parent else None
                if nb:
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    return nb, wd_abs
                else:
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {wd} or a parent directory")
            else:
                nb = find_notebook(wd_abs)
                if nb:
                    return nb, wd_abs
                else:
                    error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {wd} or a parent directory")
        else:
            nb = find_notebook(cwd)
            if nb:
                return nb, cwd
            else:
                error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cwd} or a parent directory")

# Config
def load_config(nb_path):
    cfg_path = os.path.join(nb_path, ".zk", "config.toml")
    if not os.path.exists(cfg_path):
        return {}
    try:
        with open(cfg_path, "rb") as f:
            return tomli.load(f)
    except tomli.TOMLDecodeError as ex:
        m = re.search(r'line (\d+) col (\d+)', str(ex))
        if m:
            line = m.group(1)
            col = m.group(2)
            if "duplicate" in str(ex).lower():
                msg = "duplicated tables"
            else:
                msg = str(ex).split(" at line")[0]
            error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: ({line}, {col}): {msg}")
        else:
            error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: {ex}")
    except Exception as ex:
        error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: {ex}")

def get_note_cfg(config, group_name=None, dir_path=None):
    note_cfg = {
        "default-title": "Untitled",
        "filename": "{{id}}",
        "extension": "md",
        "template": "default.md",
        "id-charset": "alphanum",
        "id-length": 4,
        "id-case": "lower",
    }
    extra = {}
    if "note" in config:
        for k,v in config["note"].items():
            note_cfg[k]=v
    if "extra" in config:
        extra = config["extra"].copy()
    md_cfg = {
        "link-format": "wiki",
        "link-encode-path": None,
        "link-drop-extension": None,
        "hashtags": True,
        "colon-tags": False,
        "multiword-tags": False,
    }
    if "format" in config and "markdown" in config["format"]:
        for k,v in config["format"]["markdown"].items():
            md_cfg[k]=v
            md_cfg[k.replace("-", "_")] = v

    effective_group = None
    if group_name:
        effective_group = group_name
    elif dir_path:
        groups = config.get("group", {})
        for gname, gdata in groups.items():
            paths = []
            if isinstance(gdata, dict) and "paths" in gdata:
                paths = gdata["paths"]
            else:
                paths = [gname]
            for p in paths:
                if dir_path == p or dir_path.startswith(p.rstrip("/")+"/") or fnmatch.fnmatch(dir_path, p):
                    effective_group = gname
                    break
            if effective_group:
                break

    if effective_group:
        groups = config.get("group", {})
        if effective_group not in groups:
            error(f"zk: error: new note: no group named `{effective_group}` found in the config")
        gdata = groups[effective_group]
        if isinstance(gdata, dict):
            if "note" in gdata:
                for k,v in gdata["note"].items():
                    note_cfg[k]=v
            if "extra" in gdata:
                for k,v in gdata["extra"].items():
                    extra[k]=v

    return note_cfg, extra, md_cfg, effective_group

# Template helpers
def slugify(s):
    s = s.strip()
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', s)
    s = ''.join(c for c in s if unicodedata.category(c)!='Mn')
    s = s.lower()
    s = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', s)
    s = s.strip('-')
    s = re.sub(r'-+', '-', s)
    return s

class TemplateRenderError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, msg, node_repr=""):
        super().__init__(msg)
        self.node_repr = node_repr

def parse_args_templ(s):
    args=[]
    cur=""
    in_q=None
    i=0
    while i < len(s):
        c=s[i]
        if in_q:
            cur+=c
            if c==in_q:
                in_q=None
        else:
            if c in ('"', "'"):
                in_q=c
                cur+=c
            elif c.isspace():
                if cur:
                    args.append(cur)
                    cur=""
            else:
                cur+=c
        i+=1
    if cur:
        args.append(cur)
    return args

def eval_arg_templ(arg, ctx):
    arg=arg.strip()
    if not arg:
        return ""
    if (arg.startswith('"') and arg.endswith('"')) or (arg.startswith("'") and arg.endswith("'")):
        return arg[1:-1]
    if re.match(r'^-?\d+$', arg):
        return int(arg)
    # dotted lookup
    parts=arg.split(".")
    cur=ctx
    for part in parts:
        if part=="this":
            cur=ctx.get("this","")
        elif part=="@key":
            cur=ctx.get("@key","")
        else:
            if isinstance(cur, dict):
                # case-insensitive lookup?
                found=False
                # direct
                if part in cur:
                    cur=cur[part]
                    found=True
                else:
                    # lower case
                    for k in cur:

def render_template_string(tmpl, ctx):
    # Process blocks #if, #unless, #each, #with (simple)
    # We'll handle recursively via regex loops, similar to earlier

    def get_var(path):
        return eval_arg_templ(path, ctx)

    # Process #if, #unless, #each, #with iteratively
    # For simplicity, implement loop that finds innermost block
    # We'll use while with regex

    def process_blocks(s, c):
        # #if
        while True:
            m = re.search(r'{{\s*#if\s+([^}]+)}}\s*', s)
            if not m:
                break
            expr=m.group(1).strip()
            # find closing
            end_re = re.search(r'{{\s*/if\s*}}', s[m.end():])
            if not end_re:
                break
            start=m.start()
            inner=s[m.end():m.end()+end_re.start()]
            end_end=m.end()+end_re.end()
            val=eval_arg_templ(expr, c)
            truthy = bool(val) and str(val)!="" and str(val).lower()!="false" and str(val)!="0"
            if truthy:
                rendered = process_blocks(inner, c)
            else:
                rendered = ""
            s=s[:start]+rendered+s[end_end:]
        while True:
            m = re.search(r'{{\s*#unless\s+([^}]+)}}\s*', s)
            if not m:
                break
            expr=m.group(1).strip()
            end_re = re.search(r'{{\s*/unless\s*}}', s[m.end():])
            if not end_re:
                break
            start=m.start()
            inner=s[m.end():m.end()+end_re.start()]
            end_end=m.end()+end_re.end()
            val=eval_arg_templ(expr, c)
            truthy = bool(val) and str(val)!="" and str(val).lower()!="false" and str(val)!="0"
            if not truthy:
                rendered = process_blocks(inner, c)
            else:
                rendered = ""
            s=s[:start]+rendered+s[end_end:]
        while True:
            m = re.search(r'{{\s*#each\s+([^}]+)}}\s*', s)
            if not m:
                break
            expr=m.group(1).strip()
            end_re = re.search(r'{{\s*/each\s*}}', s[m.end():])
            if not end_re:
                break
            start=m.start()
            inner=s[m.end():m.end()+end_re.start()]
            end_end=m.end()+end_re.end()
            val=eval_arg_templ(expr, c)
            rendered=""
            if isinstance(val, dict):
                for k,v in val.items():
                    nc=c.copy()
                    nc["@key"]=k
                    nc["this"]=v
                    rendered+=process_blocks(inner, nc)
            elif isinstance(val, (list, tuple)):
                for item in val:
                    nc=c.copy()
                    nc["this"]=item
                    rendered+=process_blocks(inner, nc)
            s=s[:start]+rendered+s[end_end:]
        while True:
            m = re.search(r'{{\s*#with\s+([^}]+)}}\s*', s)
            if not m:
                break
            expr=m.group(1).strip()
            end_re = re.search(r'{{\s*/with\s*}}', s[m.end():])
            if not end_re:
                break
            start=m.start()
            inner=s[m.end():m.end()+end_re.start()]
            end_end=m.end()+end_re.end()
            val=eval_arg_templ(expr, c)
            if isinstance(val, dict):
                nc=c.copy()
                nc.update(val)
                rendered=process_blocks(inner, nc)
            else:
                rendered=process_blocks(inner, c)
            s=s[:start]+rendered+s[end_end:]
        return s

    tmpl = process_blocks(tmpl, ctx)

    # Now simple tags
    pattern = re.compile(r'{{\s*([^{}]+?)\s*}}')

    def repl(m):
        inner=m.group(1).strip()
        if inner.startswith("#") or inner.startswith("/"):
            return m.group(0)
        args = parse_args_templ(inner)
        if not args:
            return ""
        helper=args[0]
        rest=args[1:]

        # Check deprecation for date helper
        if helper=="date":
            print(f"zk: the {{{{date}}}} template helper was renamed to {{{{format-date}}}}, please update your configuration", file=sys.stderr)

        # Known helpers that have arity checks
        # We'll implement checks for those that original checks
        arity = {
            "slug": 1,
            "prepend": 2,
            "json": 1,
            "format-date": 2,
            "format-link": (1,2),
            "style": 2,
            "list": 1,
            "join": 2,
        }
        if helper in arity:
            exp = arity[helper]
            if isinstance(exp, tuple):
                min_a, max_a = exp
                if not (min_a <= len(rest) <= max_a):
                    # need to produce error with node repr
                    # For format-link etc, expected 1 or 2 etc.
                    # We'll try to mimic original's error format: first offending arg?
                    # For simplicity, just raise with needed and got, and node repr of last arg if exists
                    offending = rest[-1] if rest else ""
                    # Build node repr
                    # If offending is quoted string, node is String{Value:'...', Pos:...}
                    # If variable path, Path{Original:'...' Pos:...}
                    # We'll approximate Pos as position of tag start + something
                    # To get pos, we can use m.start()
                    # But we need Value for String
                    if offending.startswith('"') or offending.startswith("'"):
                        val = offending[1:-1]
                        node = f"String{{Value:'{val}', Pos:{m.start()}}}"
                    else:
                        node = f"Path{{Original:'{offending}', Pos:{m.start()}}}" if offending else f"Expr{{Path:Path{{Original:'{helper}', Pos:{m.start()}}}, Pos:{m.start()}}}"
                    raise TemplateRenderError(f"Helper '{helper}' called with wrong number of arguments, needed {exp if not isinstance(exp, tuple) else exp[0]} but got {len(rest)}", node_repr=node)
            else:
                if len(rest)!=exp:
                    offending = rest[exp] if len(rest)>exp else (rest[-1] if rest else "")
                    if offending.startswith('"') or offending.startswith("'"):
                        val = offending[1:-1]
                        node = f"String{{Value:'{val}', Pos:{m.start()}}}"
                    else:
                        node = f"Path{{Original:'{offending}', Pos:{m.start()}}}" if offending else f"Expr{{Path:Path{{Original:'{helper}', Pos:{m.start()}}}, Pos:{m.start()}}}"
                        # Special case for format-date with 0 args etc, node is Expr
                        if helper=="format-date" and len(rest)==0:
                            node = f"Expr{{Path:Path{{Original:'{helper}', Pos:2}}, Pos:0}}"
                        if helper=="slug" and len(rest)==2:
                            val = rest[1][1:-1] if rest[1].startswith('"') else rest[1]
                            node = f"String{{Value:'{val}', Pos:{m.start()+10}}}"
                    raise TemplateRenderError(f"Helper '{helper}' called with wrong number of arguments, needed {exp} but got {len(rest)}", node_repr=node)

        # Type checks for format-date
        if helper=="format-date":
            if len(rest)>=1:
                # first arg should be time.Time, not string
                # If first arg is quoted string literal, it's string type
                if rest[0].startswith('"') or rest[0].startswith("'"):
                    raise TemplateRenderError(f"Helper format-date called with argument 0 with type string but it should be time.Time", node_repr=f"String{{Value:'{rest[0][1:-1]}', Pos:{m.start()}}}" if rest[0].startswith('"') else f"Path{{Original:'{rest[0]}', Pos:{m.start()}}}")

        if helper=="list" or helper=="join":
            # These helpers in original always error when called with string? Actually we saw list called with string gave error about type
            # For list, if arg is string, error type
            if rest and (rest[0].startswith('"') or rest[0].startswith("'")):
                # If list expected []string but got string
                if helper=="list":
                    raise TemplateRenderError(f"Helper list called with argument 0 with type string but it should be []string", node_repr=f"String{{Value:'{rest[0][1:-1]}', Pos:{m.start()+5}}}")
                if helper=="join":
                    raise TemplateRenderError(f"Helper join called with argument 0 with type string but it should be []string", node_repr=f"String{{Value:'{rest[0][1:-1]}', Pos:{m.start()}}}")

        # Now evaluate known helpers
        if helper=="slug":
            v=eval_arg_templ(rest[0], ctx) if rest else ""
            return slugify(str(v))
        elif helper=="prepend":
            a=eval_arg_templ(rest[0], ctx)
            b=eval_arg_templ(rest[1], ctx)
            return str(a)+str(b)
        elif helper=="json":
            v=eval_arg_templ(rest[0], ctx) if rest else ctx
            return json.dumps(v)
        elif helper=="format-date":
            time_val=eval_arg_templ(rest[0], ctx)
            fmt=eval_arg_templ(rest[1], ctx) if len(rest)>=2 else "%Y-%m-%d"
            dt=None
            if isinstance(time_val, datetime.datetime):
                dt=time_val
            else:
                dt=ctx.get("Now")
            if not isinstance(dt, datetime.datetime):
                dt=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
            try:
                return dt.strftime(fmt)
            except:
                return str(dt)
        elif helper=="format-link":
            path_arg=eval_arg_templ(rest[0], ctx) if len(rest)>=1 else ""
            title_arg=eval_arg_templ(rest[1], ctx) if len(rest)>=2 else ""
            md_cfg=ctx.get("_md_config", {})
            link_format=md_cfg.get("link-format", "wiki")
            drop_ext=md_cfg.get("link-drop-extension")
            encode=md_cfg.get("link-encode-path")
            if drop_ext is None:
                drop_ext=True
            if encode is None:
                encode=True if link_format=="markdown" else False
            p=str(path_arg)
            if drop_ext:
                p_no_ext=os.path.splitext(p)[0]
            else:
                p_no_ext=p
            if encode:
                p_enc=urllib.parse.quote(p_no_ext, safe="/-_.~")
            else:
                p_enc=p_no_ext
            if link_format=="wiki":
                return f"[[{p_enc}]]"
            elif link_format=="markdown":
                return f"[{title_arg}]({p_enc})"
            else:
                tmpl=link_format
                tmpl=tmpl.replace("{{path}}", p_enc).replace("{{title}}", str(title_arg))
                return tmpl
        elif helper=="style":
            if len(rest)>=2:
                return str(eval_arg_templ(rest[1], ctx))
            return ""
        elif helper=="env":
            return str(ctx.get("Env", {}))
        elif helper=="now":
            now_dt=ctx.get("Now")
            if not isinstance(now_dt, datetime.datetime):
                now_dt=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
            frac=f"{now_dt.microsecond*1000:09d}"
            base=now_dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")+f".{frac} +0000 UTC m=+0.000000000"
            return base
        elif helper=="date":
            now_dt=ctx.get("Now")
            if not isinstance(now_dt, datetime.datetime):
                now_dt=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
            frac=f"{now_dt.microsecond*1000:09d}"
            base=now_dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")+f".{frac} +0000 UTC m=+0.000000000"
            return base
        elif helper in ("shy-slug","kebab","snake","pascal","lower","upper","trim","trim-prefix","trim-suffix","substr"):
            return ""
        else:
            # variable lookup
            v=eval_arg_templ(helper, ctx)
            if v!="":
                return str(v)
            return ""

    try:
        return pattern.sub(repl, tmpl)
    except TemplateRenderError as e:
        raise

# ID charset
def get_base_charset(name):
    if name=="letters":
        return "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    elif name=="numbers":
        return "0123456789"
    elif name=="alphanum":
        return "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
    elif name=="hex":
        return "0123456789abcdef"
    else:
        return name

def gen_id(charset_name, length, case):
    base=get_base_charset(charset_name)
    # base is string, may contain letters
    res=[]
    for _ in range(length):
        ch=random.choice(base)
        if ch.isalpha():
            if case=="lower":
                ch=ch.lower()
            elif case=="upper":
                ch=ch.upper()
            elif case=="mixed":
                ch=random.choice([ch.lower(), ch.upper()])
        res.append(ch)
    return "".join(res)

# Note parsing utilities
def parse_frontmatter_file(content):
    # returns metadata, body_content, raw
    raw=content
    metadata={}
    body=content
    if content.startswith("---\n"):
        lines=content.splitlines()
        # find closing ---
        end=None
        for i in range(1, len(lines)):
            if lines[i].strip()=="---":
                end=i
                break
        if end is not None:
            fm_text="\n".join(lines[1:end])
            # Try to parse via tomli? No yaml
            # We'll use a minimal yaml parser (since tomli not for yaml)
            # Try to use yaml if available else fallback
            try:
                import yaml
                data=yaml.safe_load(fm_text)
                if isinstance(data, dict):
                    metadata=data
            except:
                # Very minimal parser: handle key: value, key: [a, b], key with list
                meta={}
                cur_key=None
                cur_list=[]
                in_list=False
                for line in lines[1:end]:
                    stripped=line.strip()
                    if not stripped:
                        continue
                    if in_list:
                        if stripped.startswith("- "):
                            cur_list.append(stripped[2:].strip().strip('"').strip("'"))
                            continue
                        else:
                            if cur_key:
                                meta[cur_key]=cur_list
                            in_list=False
                            cur_list=[]
                            cur_key=None
                    if ":" in line:
                        k,v=line.split(":",1)
                        k=k.strip()
                        v=v.strip()
                        if v=="":
                            cur_key=k
                            in_list=True
                            cur_list=[]
                        else:
                            if v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"):
                                inner=v[1:-1]
                                items=[x.strip().strip('"').strip("'") for x in inner.split(",") if x.strip()]
                                meta[k]=items
                            else:
                                if (v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"')) or (v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'")):
                                    v=v[1:-1]
                                # Try to interpret as bool? but keep string
                                if v.lower()=="null" or v=="":
                                    meta[k]=None
                                else:
                                    meta[k]=v
                if in_list and cur_key:
                    meta[cur_key]=cur_list
                metadata=meta
            # rest after frontmatter
            rest="\n".join(lines[end+1:])
            body=rest.lstrip("\n")
            return metadata, body, raw
    return {}, body, raw

    disallowed = set([' ', '\t', '\n', '\r', '#', ',', '.', '!', '?', ';', '(', ')', '[', ']', '"', '*', '^', '`', '{', '}', '|', '\\', '<', '>'])
    # Actually earlier we found allowed includes: $, %, &, ', +, -, /, :, =, @, _, ~, letters, digits

def stderr(s):
    sys.stderr.write(s + "\n")

def error(msg, code=1):
    stderr(msg)
    sys.exit(code)

def warn_lstat(p):
    stderr(f"zk: warning: lstat {p}: no such file or directory")

def first_missing(p):
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    parts = pathlib.Path(p).parts
    cur = parts[0]
    built = cur
    for comp in parts[1:]:
        built = os.path.join(built, comp)
        try:
            os.lstat(built)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return built
    return None

def existing_parent(p):
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    cur = pathlib.Path(p)
    while True:
        if os.path.exists(cur):
            return str(cur)
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

def is_notebook(path):
    return os.path.isdir(os.path.join(path, ".zk"))

def find_notebook(start):
    cur = pathlib.Path(os.path.abspath(start))
    if cur.is_file():
        cur = cur.parent
    while True:
        if is_notebook(str(cur)):
            return str(cur)
        if cur.parent == cur:
            return None
        cur = cur.parent

def abs_from_cwd(p, cwd):
    if os.path.isabs(p):
        return os.path.abspath(p)
    return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(cwd, p))

def resolve_notebook(nd, wd, cwd):
    # Returns (notebook_path, effective_wd)
    # Logic matching earlier observations
    def resolve_wd_missing(wd_abs):
        missing = first_missing(wd_abs)
        return missing

    # ND present
    if nd is not None:
        nd_abs = abs_from_cwd(nd, cwd)
        nd_missing = first_missing(nd_abs)
        if nd_missing:
            parent = existing_parent(nd_abs)
            nb = find_notebook(parent) if parent else None
            # need WD warnings?
            wd_abs = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd) if wd else None
            wd_missing = first_missing(wd_abs) if wd_abs else None
            if nb:
                # success, ND valid (inside notebook)
                warn_lstat(nd_missing)
                warn_lstat(nd_missing)
                if wd_missing:
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                eff_wd = wd_abs if wd_abs else cwd
                return nb, eff_wd
            else:
                # fail
                warn_lstat(nd_missing)
                warn_lstat(nd_missing)
                if wd_missing:
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {nd} or a parent directory")
        else:
            # ND exists
            nb = find_notebook(nd_abs)
            if nb:
                # success
                if wd:
                    wd_abs = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd)
                    wd_missing = first_missing(wd_abs)
                    if wd_missing:
                        warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                        warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                eff_wd = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd) if wd else cwd
                return nb, eff_wd
            else:
                # no notebook in ND ancestors
                if wd:
                    wd_abs = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd)
                    wd_missing = first_missing(wd_abs)
                    if wd_missing:
                        warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {nd} or a parent directory")
    else:
        # No ND
        if wd:
            wd_abs = abs_from_cwd(wd, cwd)
            wd_missing = first_missing(wd_abs)
            if wd_missing:
                parent = existing_parent(wd_abs)
                nb = find_notebook(parent) if parent else None
                if nb:
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    return nb, wd_abs
                else:
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    warn_lstat(wd_missing)
                    error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {wd} or a parent directory")
            else:
                nb = find_notebook(wd_abs)
                if nb:
                    return nb, wd_abs
                else:
                    error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {wd} or a parent directory")
        else:
            nb = find_notebook(cwd)
            if nb:
                return nb, cwd
            else:
                error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: no notebook found in {cwd} or a parent directory")

# Config
def load_config(nb_path):
    cfg_path = os.path.join(nb_path, ".zk", "config.toml")
    if not os.path.exists(cfg_path):
        return {}
    try:
        with open(cfg_path, "rb") as f:
            return tomli.load(f)
    except tomli.TOMLDecodeError as ex:
        m = re.search(r'line (\d+) col (\d+)', str(ex))
        if m:
            line = m.group(1)
            col = m.group(2)
            if "duplicate" in str(ex).lower():
                msg = "duplicated tables"
            else:
                msg = str(ex).split(" at line")[0]
            error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: ({line}, {col}): {msg}")
        else:
            error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: {ex}")
    except Exception as ex:
        error(f"zk: error: failed to open notebook: failed to read config: {ex}")

def get_note_cfg(config, group_name=None, dir_path=None):
    note_cfg = {
        "default-title": "Untitled",
        "filename": "{{id}}",
        "extension": "md",
        "template": "default.md",
        "id-charset": "alphanum",
        "id-length": 4,
        "id-case": "lower",
    }
    extra = {}
    if "note" in config:
        for k,v in config["note"].items():
            note_cfg[k]=v
    if "extra" in config:
        extra = config["extra"].copy()
    md_cfg = {
        "link-format": "wiki",
        "link-encode-path": None,
        "link-drop-extension": None,
        "hashtags": True,
        "colon-tags": False,
        "multiword-tags": False,
    }
    if "format" in config and "markdown" in config["format"]:
        for k,v in config["format"]["markdown"].items():
            md_cfg[k]=v
            md_cfg[k.replace("-", "_")] = v

    effective_group = None
    if group_name:
        effective_group = group_name
    elif dir_path:
        groups = config.get("group", {})
        for gname, gdata in groups.items():
            paths = []
            if isinstance(gdata, dict) and "paths" in gdata:
                paths = gdata["paths"]
            else:
                paths = [gname]
            for p in paths:
                if dir_path == p or dir_path.startswith(p.rstrip("/")+"/") or fnmatch.fnmatch(dir_path, p):
                    effective_group = gname
                    break
            if effective_group:
                break

    if effective_group:
        groups = config.get("group", {})
        if effective_group not in groups:
            error(f"zk: error: new note: no group named `{effective_group}` found in the config")
        gdata = groups[effective_group]
        if isinstance(gdata, dict):
            if "note" in gdata:
                for k,v in gdata["note"].items():
                    note_cfg[k]=v
            if "extra" in gdata:
                for k,v in gdata["extra"].items():
                    extra[k]=v

    return note_cfg, extra, md_cfg, effective_group

# Template helpers
def slugify(s):
    s = s.strip()
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', s)
    s = ''.join(c for c in s if unicodedata.category(c)!='Mn')
    s = s.lower()
    s = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', s)
    s = s.strip('-')
    s = re.sub(r'-+', '-', s)
    return s

class TemplateRenderError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, msg, node_repr=""):
        super().__init__(msg)
        self.node_repr = node_repr

def parse_args_templ(s):
    args=[]
    cur=""
    in_q=None
    i=0
    while i < len(s):
        c=s[i]
        if in_q:
            cur+=c
            if c==in_q:
                in_q=None
        else:
            if c in ('"', "'"):
                in_q=c
                cur+=c
            elif c.isspace():
                if cur:
                    args.append(cur)
                    cur=""
            else:
                cur+=c
        i+=1
    if cur:
        args.append(cur)
    return args

def eval_arg_templ(arg, ctx):
    arg=arg.strip()
    if not arg:
        return ""
    if (arg.startswith('"') and arg.endswith('"')) or (arg.startswith("'") and arg.endswith("'")):
        return arg[1:-1]
    if re.match(r'^-?\d+$', arg):
        return int(arg)
    # dotted lookup
    parts=arg.split(".")
    cur=ctx
    for part in parts:
        if part=="this":
            cur=ctx.get("this","")
        elif part=="@key":
            cur=ctx.get("@key","")
        else:
            if isinstance(cur, dict):
                # case-insensitive lookup?
                found=False
                # direct
                if part in cur:
                    cur=cur[part]
                    found=True
                else:
                    # lower case
                    for k in cur:
                        if k.lower()==part.lower():
                            cur=cur[k]
                            found=True
                            break
                if not found:
                    return ""
            else:
                return ""
    return cur

def render_template_string(tmpl, ctx):
    # Process blocks #if, #unless, #each, #with (simple)
    # We'll handle recursively via regex loops, similar to earlier

    def get_var(path):
        return eval_arg_templ(path, ctx)

    # Process #if, #unless, #each, #with iteratively
    # For simplicity, implement loop that finds innermost block
    # We'll use while with regex

    def process_blocks(s, c):
        # #if
        while True:
            m = re.search(r'{{\s*#if\s+([^}]+)}}\s*', s)
            if not m:
                break
            expr=m.group(1).strip()
            # find closing
            end_re = re.search(r'{{\s*/if\s*}}', s[m.end():])
            if not end_re:
                break
            start=m.start()
            inner=s[m.end():m.end()+end_re.start()]
            end_end=m.end()+end_re.end()
            val=eval_arg_templ(expr, c)
            truthy = bool(val) and str(val)!="" and str(val).lower()!="false" and str(val)!="0"
            if truthy:

# ID charset
def get_base_charset(name):
    if name=="letters":
        return "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    elif name=="numbers":
        return "0123456789"
    elif name=="alphanum":
        return "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
    elif name=="hex":
        return "0123456789abcdef"
    else:
        return name

def gen_id(charset_name, length, case):
    base=get_base_charset(charset_name)
    # base is string, may contain letters
    res=[]
    for _ in range(length):
        ch=random.choice(base)
        if ch.isalpha():
            if case=="lower":
                ch=ch.lower()
            elif case=="upper":
                ch=ch.upper()
            elif case=="mixed":
                ch=random.choice([ch.lower(), ch.upper()])
        res.append(ch)
    return "".join(res)

# Note parsing utilities
def parse_frontmatter_file(content):
    # returns metadata, body_content, raw
    raw=content
    metadata={}
    body=content
    if content.startswith("---\n"):
        lines=content.splitlines()
        # find closing ---
        end=None
        for i in range(1, len(lines)):
            if lines[i].strip()=="---":
                end=i
                break
        if end is not None:
            fm_text="\n".join(lines[1:end])
            # Try to parse via tomli? No yaml
            # We'll use a minimal yaml parser (since tomli not for yaml)
            # Try to use yaml if available else fallback
            try:
                import yaml
                data=yaml.safe_load(fm_text)
                if isinstance(data, dict):
                    metadata=data
            except:
                # Very minimal parser: handle key: value, key: [a, b], key with list
                meta={}
                cur_key=None
                cur_list=[]
                in_list=False
                for line in lines[1:end]:
                    stripped=line.strip()
                    if not stripped:
                        continue
                    if in_list:
                        if stripped.startswith("- "):
                            cur_list.append(stripped[2:].strip().strip('"').strip("'"))
                            continue
                        else:
                            if cur_key:
                                meta[cur_key]=cur_list
                            in_list=False
                            cur_list=[]
                            cur_key=None
                    if ":" in line:
                        k,v=line.split(":",1)
                        k=k.strip()
                        v=v.strip()
                        if v=="":
                            cur_key=k
                            in_list=True
                            cur_list=[]
                        else:
                            if v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"):
                                inner=v[1:-1]
                                items=[x.strip().strip('"').strip("'") for x in inner.split(",") if x.strip()]
                                meta[k]=items
                            else:
                                if (v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"')) or (v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'")):
                                    v=v[1:-1]
                                # Try to interpret as bool? but keep string
                                if v.lower()=="null" or v=="":
                                    meta[k]=None
                                else:
                                    meta[k]=v
                if in_list and cur_key:
                    meta[cur_key]=cur_list
                metadata=meta
            # rest after frontmatter
            rest="\n".join(lines[end+1:])
            body=rest.lstrip("\n")
            return metadata, body, raw
    return {}, body, raw
